exposure: Patients who did not undergo labor
cohort: Patients with live singleton births at or after 24 weeks of gestation who had a prior classical cesarean delivery or a low transverse cesarean delivery from the 2016-2019 National Inpatient Sample database
finding: Prior classical cesarean delivery was associated with a higher risk of uterine rupture and severe maternal morbidity in subsequent pregnancies, compared with prior low transverse cesarean delivery, even after accounting for patients' clinical, sociodemographic, and hospital characteristics.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery occurred in 95.5% of patients with prior classical cesarean compared with 91.3% of those with prior low transverse delivery, and uterine rupture occurred in 1.1% and 0.3%, respectively.
